pathophysiology.summary: Valve disease obstructs (stenosis) or leaks (regurgitation), overloading the ventricles. Severe disease causes symptoms, ventricular dysfunction and death; intervention relieves the load before irreversible damage.
keyMechanisms: Aortic stenosis raises LV pressure load → hypertrophy, angina, syncope, heart failure.
Regurgitation causes volume overload → dilatation; end-systolic diameter thresholds signal decompensation (NICE NG208).
Symptomatic severe disease warrants intervention (NICE NG208).

symptoms: Breathlessness, angina, syncope or reduced exercise tolerance.
physicalSigns: Murmur (ejection systolic with reduced second sound in severe AS).
redFlags: Syncope or chest pain with an aortic stenosis murmur — urgent assessment
Pregnancy with significant valve disease — specialist (NICE NG208)

clinicalManagement.title: Indication and choice
actions: Offer intervention for symptomatic severe valve disease (NICE NG208).
Asymptomatic severe AS: consider if Vmax above 5 m/s, valve area below 0.6 cm² or LVEF below 55%.
Surgery first line at low or intermediate surgical risk; TAVI for non-bicuspid severe AS at high risk or when surgery is unsuitable (NICE NG208).
Asymptomatic severe disease not yet needing intervention: review every 6–12 months with echo; mild AS/MS echo every 3–5 years.

clinicalManagement.title: After intervention
actions: No anticoagulation after surgical biological valve unless another indication; consider aspirin (or clopidogrel) after TAVI (NICE NG208 1.7).

clinicalManagement.title: Pre-operative assessment
actions: Grade surgery (minor, intermediate, major/complex) and ASA status; order only the tests NICE NG45 lists for that combination.
Do not routinely order chest X-ray, urine dipstick, sickle tests or HbA1c in people without diabetes (NICE NG45).
Discuss stopping smoking and reducing alcohol; manage iron-deficiency anaemia (NICE NG180).
Make an individual anticoagulant plan if the person takes anticoagulants (NICE NG45).

clinicalManagement.title: VTE prophylaxis
actions: Cardiac surgery: consider mechanical prophylaxis; consider LMWH for at least 7 days if not otherwise anticoagulated (NICE NG89 1.15).

clinicalManagement.title: Surgical antibiotic prophylaxis (MOH Protocol-015)
actions: Cardiac procedures: screen and decolonise MRSA; cefazolin 2 g IV (3 g if 120 kg or more) within 60 min (MOH p. 1).
Allergy: clindamycin 900 mg (60 min) or vancomycin 15 mg/kg (max 2 g) within 120 min (MOH p. 1).
Re-dose cefazolin every 4 h (or clindamycin every 6 h) if surgery lasts more than 4 h or blood loss exceeds 1,500 mL (MOH p. 1).
Stop prophylaxis within 24 h of the end of surgery, even with drains or catheters (MOH p. 4).

patientEducation: Report new breathlessness, chest pain or syncope.
lifestyleAndDiet: Stop smoking and reduce alcohol before surgery (NICE NG180).
Stay active; prehabilitation exercises where advised.
dischargeCriteria: Pain controlled with oral analgesia; eating, drinking and mobilising.
Wound satisfactory; VTE prophylaxis plan and follow-up arranged.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Post-operative review per surgical team; return immediately with fever, wound redness, calf swelling, breathlessness or chest pain.
